MKCinema ships no channels of its own. Add a playlist from a TV service you subscribe to (M3U, Xtream or XMLTV), or install a Stremio addon that provides TV channels.
Ninety seconds from the middle of one film, then the next, from sources your debrid service already has cached. Keep watching from that second, or start from the top.
Signed up with Facebook? Set a Stremio password first. If your browser blocks the call to Stremio, MKCinema relays it through its own server without storing anything.
Hides sources dubbed only in other languages, so Smart Play and auto-switch never pick them. Releases that name no language, or MULTi and Dual Audio releases, stay listed.
Swaps posters for RatingPosterDB versions with ratings printed on them. Uses the free key unless you add your own. A poster RPDB does not have falls back to the normal one.
A debrid service turns the torrent links your addons find into fast, direct streams that start instantly. MKCinema works with all the major ones, so use whichever you prefer:
Torrent results get a Debrid badge (Instant when your service reports them cached) and Smart Play prefers them. If more than one key is saved, the one you added first is used.
MKCinema ships no movies of its own. Stream addons you choose and trust supply the sources, just like Stremio. Install them from the addon manager by pasting their manifest link.
Hides programs, archives, samples, other episodes and files far too small to be the film. Cinema recordings, a different year or a small file for the quality drop down the list with a note.
Play what you already own. Films and episodes on your own Plex, Jellyfin or Emby server show up as sources next to your addons, and Smart Play picks them first. Sign-ins stay on this device.
MKCinema is a client for the open Stremio addon protocol. Metadata from Cinemeta, subtitles from OpenSubtitles. It ships no streams of its own: playable sources come from the addons you install.

Desktop players on Linux have no web link, so MKCinema saves an .m3u playlist your default player opens. Saved for Linux and synced to your account. Torrents, local files and trailers always play here.

Once per visit, Cloudflare Web Analytics counts the page, the site you came from, browser, country and load speed. No cookies, no IDs, nothing about your addons, keys or what you watch. Off sends nothing.

MKCinema has no database of famous scenes, and none is pretended. Each scene starts at a point between about a third and three quarters of the way into the film, past the opening and well before the credits.

Opens a new GitHub issue with a short diagnostic filled in (version, device, settings, recent errors). It never includes keys, passwords or links. The diagnostic is also copied, so you can paste it anywhere.

Opens the stream in an installed Android app, the same way Stremio does. If the app is missing, the Play Store opens. Saved for Android and synced to your account. Torrents, local files and trailers always play here.

Only sources your debrid service already has cached, in formats this device can play, are used. MKCinema looks up one film at a time and buffers only the next scene, so your addons and your debrid account are never flooded.

MKCinema is built and kept online by Drake Christopher, with no ads, no cookies and no profiles. Donations pay for hosting, the domain and the hours that go into new features. If it has made your movie nights better, a coffee’s worth goes a long way.
Menus, buttons and settings. Titles and descriptions come from your addons and stay in the language they send.

MKCinema has no catalog of its own, so nothing can show until Cinemeta answers. This usually means the page is inside a sandbox that blocks outside requests (like the Artifact preview) or you are offline. Open the downloaded index.html in a normal browser, or run mkcinema-server.js and visit it.
From ratingposterdb.com. Stays on this device.

High is the default: raised, shimmering buttons, posters with depth, the 3D logo while a film loads, and frosted glass on desktops. Phones get all of it except the glass. If scrolling ever stutters or the battery runs low, MKCinema drops to Low by itself. Video quality is never affected.

For devices where you cannot install VLC or another player. Lists only sources this browser can play with working picture and sound (H.264 or a codec this device supports, AAC/Opus sound), and torrents only through your debrid service. Fewer sources, but the ones you see play right here.

Best for this device opens trailers in the YouTube app on TVs with the MKCinema TV app 1.2.4 or later, where they play smoothly, and plays them inside MKCinema everywhere else. Embedded trailers use youtube-nocookie.com with YouTube controls, related videos and annotations switched off, and close by themselves at the end. YouTube still shows its title, share link and More videos while a trailer is paused or touched; its terms do not allow sites to cover those. Whether an ad runs is decided by YouTube and the uploader; MKCinema does not block ads.
On a computer, hovering the seek bar shows the picture at that moment. It reads a little of the file in the background; HLS and Split Screen don’t use it.
Browsers cannot play them; they only hand off to external players.

Use your own debrid account to play torrent results instantly. Signed in, your keys travel with your account so they load on every device you sign in on; only you can read them. They are never in setup codes unless you tick that box, never shared, and only ever sent to that service (or through your own MKCinema server if your browser blocks the service).

A server on a plain http:// address can only be reached through the MKCinema companion server (Settings › Streams & addons › MKCinema proxy URL), because browsers block it from an https page. Plex servers use secure addresses by themselves.
Scrobble what you watch and keep watchlists in step. Past 80 % a title counts as watched. Connect with your own free API app; tokens stay in this browser.
